clue.text: Drink in a very soft hat outside

indicators.note: the hat is placed outside, around the very soft piece, so one encloses the other

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tippler hides a drink inside a floppy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' is a verb here, to drink habitually; 'outside' tells you the hat goes round, and tile is old British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tipple is to drink alcohol regularly, a verb as well as a noun for liquor.

clue.text: Signal for credit on food

parts.note: on tick means on credit, so tick is credit
tack is slang for food, as in hard tack

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a meal on account.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK-TACK is the hand-signalling used by British racecourse bookmakers; 'on' places credit above food in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick-tack is a system of manual semaphore by which bookies pass odds, so a kind of signalling.

clue.text: Constant or variable mathematical quantity equal to a metre converted

parts.note: at par means at an equal value
taken as written

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the following words are changed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A maths text defines a quantity equal to a metre after conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'equal' gives PAR as in 'on a par'; 'converted' turns A METRE into AMETER, the American spelling at the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a parameter is a quantity held fixed in one case but varied between cases.

clue.text: Learner frequently seen in upper room

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British L-plates
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A student is often to be found upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the space or room right under a roof, at the top of a building.

clue.text: Brave as I may possibly be and smoother

indicators.note: these words suggest the letters before them could take another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are bold and suave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may possibly be' rearranges BRAVE AS I; 'smoother' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun, a thing that smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive such as sandpaper is a material used to grind or polish surfaces flat.

clue.text: Precluding public house circle

parts.note: a bar is a pub, a public house
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A ring of drinkers keeps others out of the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Barring as a preposition means excepting or ruling out, so it serves for excluding.

clue.text: Provoke worker over struggle

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the worker above the struggle

parts.note: a worker is a worker ant, a crossword staple
to agonise is to struggle in anguish

explanation.surface: An employee is urged to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the insect, not a human employee.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to rouse their hostility, much as to provoke them.

clue.text: I'm on time for an appearance

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone arrives punctually for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the outward look or picture something presents, its appearance.

clue.text: Lay out without soft finish

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, without, as in ex dividend
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone spends without any gentle ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it, the same as to use it up.

clue.text: Dawdle like a snooker player?

definitions.meaning: to ... about is to move idly without hurry
a snooker player pots balls, so is one who pots

explanation.surface: A slow snooker player is accused of dawdling.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to mooch around idly, and a player who sinks balls is one who pots them.

clue.text: Pretty blue weed, we hear, used by the cook for thickening

definitions.text: used by the cook for thickening

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the word is judged by sound, not spelling

parts.note: the cornflower is a blue-flowered plant once a cornfield weed

explanation.surface: A cook adds a pretty blue weed to thicken a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflour is maize starch, the powder stirred into sauces and gravies to make them thick.

clue.text: Little Arthur. goes back to the politician for a walk

indicators.note: goes back means the short name is read from right to left

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Young Arthur returns to the MP for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after Arthur is a page mark; 'goes back' reverses the short name to give TRA, and 'for a walk' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk, as in a tramp across the moors.

clue.text: What the landlord calls is what the criminal does

definitions.meaning: a British pub landlord calls last orders at closing
a convict does a stretch in prison, doing porridge

explanation.surface: A pub landlord and a convict share a word.
explanation.walkthrough: A British publican shouts 'Time!' at closing; a prisoner 'does time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing is announced in a pub with that one word, and doing it means serving a jail sentence.

clue.text: Tie up money in a vegetable product

parts.note: to string something is to tie it up with cord
a bean is slang for money, as in not having a bean

explanation.surface: Someone ties up their cash in a farm product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie up money' reads as investing capital, but is two plain pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A string bean is a green pod eaten as a vegetable, a crop of the garden.

clue.text: Minister with opportunity to turn up

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for turning is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A minister seizes a chance to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROLL into LLOR beneath CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the British finance minister, a senior cabinet post.

clue.text: Understand hesitation in baseball player

parts.note: to catch a meaning is to understand it
er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A baseball player hesitates before grasping a play.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the catcher crouches behind home plate and receives the pitches.

clue.text: Sex information given to the German

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Sex education is given by a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is often used as a synonym for sex, the male or female classification.

clue.text: Fascinated by a rude omen for a change

indicators.note: the phrase asks the letters before it to be changed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely charmed by a vulgar portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges A RUDE OMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enamoured is being captivated or charmed by someone, so taken with them.

clue.text: Sudden cold spell's -getting. very warm in picture

parts.note: a cold snap is a short frosty spell, and the possessive adds an s
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: A cold snap turns to a heatwave in a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken informal photograph, a picture of a moment.

clue.text: One who cuts, the fruit right

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum, a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone trims the fruit correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pruner trims branches from trees and shrubs, a person who lops them.

clue.text: Change reserve in defeat

indicators.note: change tells the solver to alter the order of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A team brings on a substitute in a losing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change reserve' reads as a substitution in sport; 'Change' rearranges RESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or defeat, as in a military reverse.

clue.text: There is a stigma about us 24 to support

indicators.note: about means the stigma goes round the following word

parts.note: a stain is a mark of disgrace, a stigma
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims there is a slur on us to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the stigma wrap the plain word us, which sits after its first letter. The '24' on the page is a stray mark with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to hold it up, bearing its weight.

clue.text: Dry river must be safe

parts.note: sec is the French word for dry, used of wine
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river that has run dry must be safe to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure means free from danger, protected from harm.

clue.text: Good man with money on the seashore

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A good man with cash walks on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' places the saint above the money in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a shore or beach, an old poetic word for the edge of the sea.

clue.text: Jester in place of crockery :

parts.note: a teaser is someone who teases, a jester
vice means in place of, as in vice-captain

explanation.surface: A court jester takes the place of a set of dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a set of matching cups, saucers and pots, crockery for tea.

clue.text: Collect for a religious service

parts.note: Mass is the Eucharist, a church service

explanation.surface: Gathering people for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a quantity of something.

clue.text: Company work in prison

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A firm runs work schemes in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Coop is slang for a prison, as with being cooped up.

clue.text: Animal to tolerate

definitions.meaning: a large furry mammal such as a grizzly
to put up with or endure

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a large mammal; the verb means to endure something.

clue.text: Does it benefit to be sick about Virginia? Yes!

indicators.note: about means the word for being sick wraps around the state

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being ill in Virginia does any good, and says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the word for being sick wrap the state; 'Does it' and 'Yes!' are surface dressing around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a verb means to help or be of use, to profit someone.

clue.text: Two groups of soldiers go to ground; it's elemental

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, one British army corps
RE is the Royal Engineers, another British army corps
earth is ground or soil

explanation.surface: Two army units take cover in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers are corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are a group of metallic chemical elements, the lanthanides.

clue.text: Renegade upsetting red steer

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A renegade unsettles a red bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter abandons their side, as a renegade turns traitor.

clue.text: Believe in sale on trust

explanation.surface: A shopper trusts the sale terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust a claim is to accept it as true, and buying on deferred payment is buying on account.
